## Summary

- 28 cells differ, for 12 participants.
- **Spoken words:** 9 blank words are filled in (Y2-053, Y2-071, Y2-073, Y2-074, Y2-076, Y2-077, Y2-078, Y2-079, Y2-080); 1 existing word is changed (Y2-046). Blank words: 9 in the sheet in use, 0 in the received sheet.
- **Ratings:** changed for 3 participants (Y2-076, Y2-077, Y2-080). A rating is the label the models learn from, so these changes alter the analysis itself.
- **Strikethrough:** removed for Y2-076.
- **Feeling text:** filled in for Y2-071, Y2-080.
- **Subject:** filled in for 10 participants.
- **Kapoy speakers:** 10 in the sheet in use, 15 in the received sheet. The word analysis will change.

## Where the changes come from, as the group reports it

Reported by the group on 2026-10-12:

- **Ratings:** corrected from the participants' answer forms, because the first sheet had typing mistakes.
- **Words:** filled in by a group member who listened to each recording.

The pipeline cannot check these statements. The answer forms of the participants whose ratings changed (Y2-076, Y2-077, Y2-080) are the evidence for the corrected ratings and must be kept.

## Still open

For 5 participants the word in the received sheet is not the word in the name of the audio file (Y2-056, Y2-059, Y2-061, Y2-066, Y2-072). The listening review should settle these.

## What it takes to use the received sheet

- The originals stay: move the PDF in use to `data/metadata_raw/archive/` (do not delete it) and put the received PDF in its place, under the name step 00 reads.
- Run the whole pipeline again from step 00 in the pinned Python 3.12 environment. Step 06 (training) must run, because the ratings changed. It takes more than an hour.
- After that run this report disappears by itself, and every report, slide and document is rebuilt from the new results.
